chapters.title: The Best of the Best
chapters.sourcePressure: The source frames the book as a six-year Stanford Graduate School of Business research project comparing eighteen exceptional long-lasting companies against top competitors, not as a celebration of charisma or hot products.
chapters.coreMove: Judge admired companies through matched comparison, long time horizons, and surviving systems instead of founder glow or product nostalgia.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating visionary companies as a list of famous brands to admire, rather than as comparison-tested institutions whose durability has to be explained.

chapters.title: Clock Building, Not Time Telling
chapters.sourcePressure: The source rejects dependence on charismatic leaders, isolated brilliant ideas, one great program, or one gifted leader; Collins official support contrasts time-telling with clock-building and program-centered thinking with institution-centered thinking.
chapters.coreMove: Turn a brilliant answer into a reusable mechanism that keeps working when the gifted person leaves the room.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing clock building to delegation or process documentation, while leaving the institution dependent on one person for judgment.
mustNotDriftInto: whiteboard framework with no handoff test

chapters.title: More Than Profits
chapters.sourcePressure: The sidecar supports the argument that durable organizations are guided by something deeper than short-term profit, with core values and purpose defining enduring character beyond specific leaders.
chapters.coreMove: Use purpose and core values as decision constraints when a profitable option would bend the institution out of shape.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning purpose into sentimental branding or anti-profit posture instead of a practical rule for refusing profitable compromises.
mustNotDriftInto: bakery refusing a contract because it feels wrong

chapters.title: Preserve the Core/Stimulate Progress
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter title supplies the governing duality, and the source says core values and purpose endure beyond individual leaders while progress must still be stimulated.
chapters.coreMove: Separate the enduring principle from the changeable practice, then protect one by changing the other.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating preservation and progress as a compromise between old and new, instead of a disciplined separation between core and method.

chapters.title: Big Hairy Audacious Goals
chapters.sourcePressure: The sidecar supports the chapter title, the BHAG label, and the book-wide logic that visionary companies preserve a core while stimulating progress through ambition.
chapters.coreMove: Set a goal big enough to concentrate progress, but test whether its size serves the core instead of ego, spectacle, or panic.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating any huge target as visionary, when a BHAG must focus institutional effort around the core rather than inflate a leader's self-image.
mustNotDriftInto: startup announces a huge user number

chapters.title: Cult-Like Cultures
chapters.sourcePressure: The source supports strong membership defined by shared values and purpose beyond formal activity, with culture organized around real value alignment.
chapters.coreMove: Make belonging conditional on lived values, so culture selects for fit instead of merely welcoming talent.
chapters.commonMisread: Confusing cult-like culture with perks, friendliness, conformity, or blind obedience, rather than clear standards that people freely join or leave.
mustNotDriftInto: sales star laughs at service oath

chapters.title: Try a Lot of Stuff and Keep What Works
chapters.sourcePressure: The sidecar supports disciplined experimentation, institutional learning, variation, feedback, retention, and adaptation in methods without surrendering core identity.
chapters.coreMove: Run many bounded variations, read the feedback honestly, and keep only what advances the core purpose.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating experimentation as random hustle, trend-chasing, or permission to abandon the core whenever a new tactic looks exciting.
mustNotDriftInto: generic A/B test with button colors

chapters.title: Home-Grown Management
chapters.sourcePressure: The sidecar supports internal leadership development, continuity, institutional design, and avoiding dependence on imported saviors.
chapters.coreMove: Build internal leadership capacity so authority carries institutional memory and values, while still testing competence instead of rewarding tenure.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating home-grown management as promotion-from-within sentimentality or anti-outsider bias, rather than a deliberate pipeline for values plus judgment.
mustNotDriftInto: loading dock clock and outside rescuer

chapters.title: Good Enough Never Is
chapters.sourcePressure: The sidecar supports relentless improvement, demanding institutional standards, anti-complacency pressure, and the distinction between excellence and neurotic perfectionism.
chapters.coreMove: Make tolerated drift visible early and attach improvement pressure to the work, not to ego or panic.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning good enough never is into burnout, perfectionism, or leader impatience instead of a system that refuses invisible decay.

chapters.title: The End of the Beginning
chapters.sourcePressure: The final sidecar supports synthesis of the whole framework around institutions that preserve a core, stimulate progress, build systems, and outlast heroes.
chapters.coreMove: Translate admiration into architecture: core, progress mechanisms, culture, experiments, leadership pipeline, and standards that can operate after you leave.
chapters.commonMisread: Writing a recap of concepts or motivational closing instead of forcing the reader to assemble an institution-building operating system.
mustNotDriftInto: leader writing values on a blank page
